title: Network Troubleshooting: Packets, Routes and Traces
summary: Follow a web visit packet by packet, trace the route across a network, and find the one broken setting that stops a PC reaching a server. Two hands-on labs with fresh numbers every time: a packet capture to read and a simulated network with a command prompt.
outcomes: Read a packet capture and pick out ARP, DNS, the TCP three-way handshake and HTTP
Explain how routers choose a path, and how TTL and tracert reveal it
Use ipconfig, ping, tracert and routing tables to find and describe a network fault
Write a clear fault report with the fix
prerequisites: IPv4 addresses and subnet masks (the Practical Tech Skills course covers them).

modules.title: Packets: what a web visit looks like

lessons.title: ARP, DNS, TCP and HTTP in one visit
Lab: read the packet capture
lessons.intro: Filter the capture, open the packets and find the answers. Every learner gets a different capture.

lessons.title: Packets quiz
lessons.intro: Four questions on reading a capture.

questions.prompt: Which packet tells you the MAC address of the default gateway?
questions.explanation: The ARP reply says "192.168.x.1 is at <MAC>". The request only asks the question.

questions.prompt: DNS lookups normally go to which port?
questions.explanation: DNS queries use UDP port 53 (TCP 53 for large answers).

questions.prompt: In the TCP three-way handshake, which packet completes it?
questions.explanation: SYN, then SYN-ACK, then the client's ACK.

questions.prompt: A server answers "HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently". Where should the browser go next?
options: To the address in the Location header
questions.explanation: 301 means the resource moved; the new address is in the Location header.

modules.title: Routes: tracing a packet across the network

lessons.title: Lab: find the broken link
lessons.intro: Use the command prompt on PC1. Ping, trace, then read the routing tables there and back.

lessons.title: Routing quiz
lessons.intro: Four questions on routes and traces.

questions.prompt: A router has routes for 10.0.0.0/8, 10.4.0.0/16 and 0.0.0.0/0. Which does it use for 10.4.7.9?
questions.explanation: The longest matching prefix wins: /16 is more specific than /8 and /0.

questions.prompt: tracert shows r2, r4, r2, r4, r2… What is the most likely fault?
options: A routing loop: a route points the wrong way
The PC has no IP address
questions.explanation: Repeating hops mean the packet goes round until its TTL runs out.

questions.prompt: What does a router do when a packet's TTL reaches zero?
options: Drops it and sends back Time exceeded
Sends it back to the sender unchanged
questions.explanation: That reply is exactly what tracert uses to name each hop.

questions.prompt: Ping to a server times out, but tracert shows the first two routers and then only * * *. What should you check?
options: The routes back to your own network on the routers further along
questions.explanation: Requests may arrive, but replies need a route back to your network.

lessons.title: Bottom up, one test at a time

questions.prompt: ipconfig shows 169.254.12.40. What does that tell you?
options: The PC is on the internet
DHCP did not give the PC an address
questions.explanation: 169.254.x.x is the self-assigned address a PC uses when DHCP fails.

questions.prompt: You can ping 203.0.113.23 but not open results.example.net. What is the likeliest cause?
options: DNS: the name is not resolving
questions.explanation: Addresses work, names do not: check DNS with nslookup.

questions.prompt: A PC's default gateway must be…
options: A router address on the PC's own network
The server it wants to reach
questions.explanation: The PC can only hand packets to a router it can reach directly on its own network.

questions.prompt: Which command shows the MAC addresses your PC has learned?
questions.explanation: arp -a lists the IP-to-MAC entries the PC has found.

questions.prompt: Which is the best fault report?
options: Tracert stops at R2 (Destination net unreachable); R2 has no route to 192.168.42.0/24; add one via R3
questions.explanation: It says what was tested, what happened, where, and the fix.
